shill: cellular: try user-specified APN before last good APN This CL modifies shill to try a user-specified APN before the last "good" APN that resulted in a successful connection. Previously, shill always tried the last good APN first, which wasn't ideal for certain scenarios: - Users may reasonably expect that shill always treats the user-specified APN as the first choice (even through the user-specifed APN may be incorrect). - Some networks may accept multiple APNs. The last good APN that resulted in a successful connection may not always be what a user wants. Previously, shill cleared the last good APN whenever a user specifies a custom APN in order to allow the user-specified APN to be tried first. However, that only worked for the first time when the user-specified APN is provided. When shill restarted and found both user-specified APN and last good APN from the profile, the last good APN became the first choice again. This CL addresses that. Now that shill tries the user-specified APN before the last good APN, we can preserve the last good APN when a user-specified APN is provided. BUG=b:70834625 TEST=Run unit tests. TEST=Test the following on a Chromebook with cellular connectivity: 1. Connect to a network with an initial APN and verify that shill saves the APN in the Cellular.LastGoodAPN service property. 2. Disconnect from the network. 3. Specify a custom APN through the 'Mobile Data' settings UI. Verify that shill saves the APN in the Cellular.APN service property. 4. Make a new connection attempt. Verify that shill tries the custom APN (Cellular.APN) first before the the initial APN (Cellular.LastGoodAPN). 5. Repeat 1-4 with a custom APN that is incorrect. Verify that shill shill tries the custom APN first but fails to connect, and then tries the last good APN.
